properties.statement:
`answer_question` CAN ONLY REACH A QUESTION WHOSE ID IT CAN DERIVE, so any Question created by a route other than `gap_to_prompt` is PERMANENTLY UNANSWERABLE — and the loop keeps telling the next seat to follow up on it forever. Reported by api-boss (`79e8e8d5`) 2026-08-15 22:40 on the StoryFlow fleet graph; MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN SOURCE here, and their own diagnosis (i) is the right one of the three they offered.

CONFIRMED, not inferred: `detect.rs:872` `answer_question(gap_id, answer)` delegates to `set_question_status`, which at `detect.rs:888` computes `question_id = asked_question_id(gap_id)` — and that helper is pure string derivation, `format!("question:{}", gap_id.strip_prefix("gap:"))` (`detect.rs:700-702`). It then does a single `get_node(QUESTION, &question_id)` and returns not-found if that exact id is absent. THERE IS NO LOOKUP BY QUESTION ID AND NO SEARCH. A Question stored under any other id cannot be addressed by this tool at all.

THEIR MEASURED CASE: `open_questions` returned `question_id: "q:fleet_ops_as_reflow2_subproject"` alongside `gap_id: "gap:fleet_governance_has_no_executable_model"`, `status: asked`. `answer_question{question_id: ...}` was rejected as an unknown field naming `gap_id` as the legal one; `answer_question{gap_id: ...}` then answered 'no recorded question for gap'. BOTH IDENTIFIERS CAME FROM THE SAME OBJECT IN THE SAME LISTING AND NEITHER IS ACCEPTED. The derivation would have wanted `question:fleet_governance_has_no_executable_model`, which is not what their Question is called.

⭐ THE SHARP EDGE IS THE LOOP EATING ITSELF: `unanswered_questions` keeps counting it, `loop_status` keeps printing 'follow it up rather than asking again', and because the tool that implements following-up cannot close it, a later seat re-asks the user something they already ruled on — the exact failure the instruction exists to prevent, caused by the tool implementing the instruction.

THEIR WORKAROUND IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: they recorded the ruling as an accepted Decision. The substance is durable, the LINKAGE is not — nothing connects that Decision to the Question, so it still reads as open.

⚠️ REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH SHOWS THE SAME CLASS FROM THE OTHER SIDE, unresolved for days: `loop_status` here reports '1 answered question(s) never reached the design', and `open_questions` returns `question:9d265ef455a2e245` at `status: answered` carrying the user's full reply about grandfathering the 121 settled items. There the derivation MATCHES (it was made by `gap_to_prompt`) and the answer still never became design — so the gap between 'answered' and 'written in' is real independently of the id scheme.

FIXES, cheapest first, theirs and sound: (1) accept `question_id` too, since `open_questions` publishes it — the id a caller holds should work; (2) make the second rejection name what it looked for and what exists, which is the same list-the-legal-values ask already in their log from 2026-08-03; (3) let a Decision CLOSE a Question with an edge, making the linkage first-class and surviving whichever id scheme wins.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many hand-authored Questions exist across consumer graphs, and whether `withdraw_question` (same derivation, `detect.rs:878`) leaves them equally unreachable — by inspection it does, but that was not exercised.
